title: plan-fields v3 — canonical parser output
description: The canonical JSON a plan-fields parser emits over a fleet snapshot. contract_version identifies the plan-fields contract; schema_version identifies this envelope shape. References carry every extracted @blocked_by (raw/legacy/unresolved); only resolved canonical todo:// -> todo:// relations appear in edges. v3 adds the stream axis (@epic/@defect) whose GRAMMAR is owned by the epics/v1 contract and is deliberately not restated here — see depends.json.

RepoName.description: canonical repo name — the workspace-manifest key, NOT derived from the origin URL

remote_origin.description: origin URL — kept for cross-check/diagnostics only; NOT the identity source

RawTags.description: raw parsed tag values exactly as written, so grammar diagnostics never lose the original value

OwnerRef.description: Typed accountable principal parsed from operational @owner; null for missing, invalid, or transitional DEC-007 role values

owner_role.description: Transitional DEC-007 role-slug (no @); null for typed owner principals

epic.description: the @epic value exactly as written, after epics/v1 grammar validation; null when absent or malformed. The GRAMMAR PATTERN IS NOT RESTATED HERE — it belongs to urn:ecosystem:epics:v1:classification, pinned in depends.json. A second copy of the regex is exactly the drift this delegation exists to prevent.

defect.description: the @defect class, orthogonal to the epic and never a substitute for it; grammar and the closed class set belong to epics/v1 and its registry

epic_classification.description: epics/v1 four-state, at THIS layer's confidence: a single-repo parser can prove the tag is well-formed and present (`tagged`) but cannot prove the epic exists in the registry — the fleet layer, which holds epics.toml, may downgrade it to `invalid` (EP-UNKNOWN / EP-MOVED). Same split as `repo:<manifest-key>` owner validation in v2. `unavailable` never occurs on this plane: a TODO item that could not be read yields no node.

dag.description: the @dag value, present ONLY when the tag passed its grammar AND equals dags/<id>.yaml for this node's @id (a registered link plan item → executable artifact). Absent — not null — when the tag is missing or invalid; `raw` keeps the original spelling for diagnostics. OPTIONAL BY CONTRACT: no item is required to carry @dag, and its absence is never a diagnostic. The filename stem grammar here is the ItemId grammar — this pattern MUST stay equal to '^dags/' + ItemId.pattern + '\.yaml$' (the equality rule is only well-defined while the two agree; fixtures/valid/dag-id-stem-agreement pins it). Ready semantics and ledger-wide uniqueness are consumer (dispatcher) concerns, not stated here.

Reference.description: every extracted @blocked_by, resolved or not. A resolved reference ALSO appears in edges; a legacy/unresolved one never does.

raw_ref.description: the @blocked_by value exactly as written (todo:// or legacy <repo>#<slug>)

legacy_blocker_ref.description: <repo>#<slug> — set for legacy/unresolved refs; NEVER promoted to a canonical edge

Edge.description: a resolved canonical relation only (source todo:// -> resolved canonical target)

Diagnostic.description: severity here is the COMPUTED severity for this instance; diagnostics.yaml holds the default_severity policy and Phase 0b applies escalation history

code.description: PF-* codes are declared in this contract's diagnostics.yaml; EP-* codes are declared by epics/v1 and emitted verbatim — this contract does not redeclare them; the EP branch mirrors epics/v1's own code grammar so a malformed code (EP-1) fails at schema time. This is the code NAME shape, not the epic grammar — and depends.json is what forces a re-look if epics/v1 changes it
